slides.0.title: Where the vineyards are: geography and terroir
slides.0.subtitle: Morocco's wine is concentrated in its northern half
slides.1.title: From the Algerian border to the Atlantic
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The legal map
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The 14 AOGs run from Berkane in the north-east corner, on the Mediterranean and the Algerian border, to Doukkala on the Atlantic coast
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Five teaching zones
slides.1.highlights.1.content: This course groups them into the East, Meknès/Fès, the Rharb plain, Rabat/Casablanca and Doukkala. The regulations list only the 14 AOGs; these five zones are a common textbook grouping
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Meknès is the core
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The Meknès plateau is the centre of gravity. Secondary sources put its share at around half or more, but they differ, so simply remember it as the most important region
slides.1.content: Remember the layout: the East touches the Mediterranean, the core sits on an inland plateau, and the rest spreads along the Atlantic plains.
slides.2.title: A hot country: what keeps the wines fresh?
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The basic climate
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Summers are hot and dry. Sources usually describe Meknès as Mediterranean with continental influence and a marked day-night swing
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Altitude
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Meknès lies near the Middle Atlas foothills, commonly cited at about 700 m. Altitude is the main way acidity is kept here
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The Atlantic
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The coastal regions are moderated by the Atlantic. Do not apply that to Meknès, where freshness on the inland plateau comes mainly from altitude, not sea air
slides.2.content: Altitude and ocean are Morocco's two answers to heat, and different regions rely on different ones.
slides.3.title: Soil and water
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Soils
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Clay and limestone are the soils most often cited around Meknès. Details by region come mostly from secondary sources, so this course does not ask you to memorise them
slides.3.highlights.1.title: AOG: no irrigation in principle
slides.3.highlights.1.content: AOG vineyards may not be irrigated in principle; exceptions need a ministerial order and are justified by particular ecological conditions
slides.3.highlights.2.title: AOC: irrigation with a deadline
slides.3.highlights.2.content: In Coteaux de l'Atlas the deadline depends on training: 30 June for gobelet, 31 July for trellised vines
slides.3.content: In a hot, dry place water is a matter for regulation, one of the more interesting features of Moroccan rules.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Which of the 14 AOGs lies in the north-east corner, on the Algerian border and the Mediterranean?
Order 869-75 bounds Berkane by the Mediterranean to the north and the Algerian border to the east.
What mainly preserves acidity on the Meknès plateau?
It is an inland plateau near the Middle Atlas foothills.
What is the rule on irrigating AOG vineyards?
A. Not irrigated in principle; exceptions need a ministerial order
Order 869-75, article 2: non-irrigated is the rule, with exceptions for particular ecological conditions.
